prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks, in which neutral atoms trapped at a magic wavelength enabled atomic frequency measurement and comparison at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I keep optical lattice clocks with Katori and Ye as a single prize part. After the full exchange I can state the new principle the chair asks for: a trap wavelength at which the light shift cancels for the clock transition, so that thousands of neutral atoms are held in the Lamb-Dicke regime with no Doppler or recoil broadening and the statistical power of a many-atom ensemble is combined with the systematic control of a single trapped ion. That is not a better ruler (2005) and not control of one quantum system (2012); it is a different architecture, and it is the one that has been independently reproduced in Sr, Yb and Hg and compared between laboratories at about 1e-18. The citation should rest on both parts of the chain, the concept and the demonstrated performance, and on nothing that is still pending: no redefinition of the second and no thorium nuclear clock. My view of the merits is unchanged from round 1; what round 2 changed is how tightly I would word the credit and how seriously I take the discovery-of-nature objection.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection that survives the exchange is credit at the edges together with a fair question about kind. Takamoto and Ido demonstrated the first Sr lattice clock, and Lemonde, Ludlow and others contributed to the accuracy record; none is covered by a two-name prize, and I cannot verify exact priority from the supplied text. Ye's standing also rests partly on comb and cavity-stabilised-laser work that the 2005 prize and general metrology already cover, so his credit must be confined to the lattice clock. Finally, a clock is an enabling measurement tool; a member who weighs a new observational channel (IceCube) or the answer to a half-century question (Higgs) above an instrument can reasonably rank it lower, and I cannot show that this is a mistake. The support from several members who share an atomic-physics vantage, myself included, is not independent evidence of merit.

responses.point: Lindroth warns that agreement between her and me on B042 may reflect a shared atomic-physics vantage and is not evidence of merit, and she adds that reaching 1e-18 required control of blackbody shifts, higher-order light shifts and hyperpolarisability.
responses.response: I accept the warning and have tried to act on it. I therefore rest the case on evidence that does not depend on my vantage: independent reproduction in several species and laboratories and intercontinental comparisons at about 1e-18, which a non-specialist can check. I also agree that the systematic control of blackbody radiation, higher-order light shifts and hyperpolarisability is what turned the magic-wavelength idea into a real clock, and that is a reason to keep the citation on realised performance as well as on the proposal. Where I differ slightly is that the control of these shifts was shared across several groups, so the citation should say 'development' rather than imply a single decisive demonstration.

responses.point: Pearce prefers IceCube because it opens a new observational channel through a discovery of nature and argues that a two-name credit is clean and the result mature enough to stand, while accepting that source identification is partial.
responses.response: This is the strongest competing case, and the question of discovery against invention is a real judgement, not a technicality. I do not think clocks are only a refinement of earlier prizes, but I concede that a measurement capability does not change what we know about the Universe in the way a new window does. My difficulty with B029 is the credit boundary: Baikal, DUMAND, AMANDA and ANTARES are outside Halzen and Spiering, the population origin of the diffuse flux is open, and the chair has also asked whether your Fermi-LAT link affects your standing on this ballot. I therefore keep B029 as my first alternative and would vote for it if the committee prefers a discovery of nature and can write a citation that does not overclaim on sources.

responses.point: Danielsson says the Higgs discovery answered a half-century question that the 2013 prize recognised only on the theory side, and he concedes that the trio is a leadership proxy for thousands of people.
responses.response: I do not dispute the scientific weight, and I agree that a committee that honours the theory but never the experiment leaves the record lopsided. The chair asked for a principle that fixes three names, and I cannot supply a defensible one. Conception and leadership, spokesperson at discovery, and analysis leadership each give a different trio, and I cannot judge from the supplied material what each person contributed to the 2012 observation. I would not set B026 aside on merit, which is why I list it as an alternative, but I would not choose it as the public position until someone can argue the three names from specific contributions and not from seniority.

responses.point: Eriksson says the Katori and Ye pairing is not as clean as I claimed because Takamoto, Ido and Lemonde are outside it, and that the committee must decide whether the prize is for the concept or the performance.
responses.response: That is a fair correction to my word 'cleanest'; I should have said it is the least ambiguous on the shortlist and not that it is closed. My answer to your question is that the prize is for the architecture: Katori's magic-wavelength concept and the Lamb-Dicke many-atom lattice, together with its development to the 1e-18 level, where Ye's group set the accuracy and stability record. Takamoto and Ido's first demonstration is a real claim and I would acknowledge it in the committee's background note, but a first demonstration of a proposed scheme does not displace its proposer, and the three-name limit forces a choice either way. I would apply the same discipline to B037, where I make no judgement about Yuasa and Djayaprawira.

responses.point: Mehlig accepts B042 as the best-supported candidate but asks what new principle the lattice clock adds beyond a superb implementation of what the 2005 and 2012 prizes covered, and says he would take B042 as a compromise.
responses.response: The principle is the magic wavelength: a trap whose light shift cancels for the clock transition, which removes the usual trade between holding atoms and perturbing them. Neither the comb, which measures optical frequencies, nor ion control, which isolates one particle, supplies that, and the many-atom Lamb-Dicke ensemble is what gives the stability that single-ion clocks cannot reach. I accept your point that B034 is a mature statistical-physics case with a precise experimental test, but I think the Parisi and exact-solution credit problem is larger than for B042, and I welcome your willingness to treat B042 as a compromise.

uncertainties: Whether Takamoto, Ido or Lemonde have a priority claim that a two-name credit cannot cover, and how a citation can be worded to remain accurate without naming them.
Whether members outside atomic physics see the magic-wavelength lattice as a new principle or as an implementation of capabilities honoured in 2005 and 2012.
Whether the committee should weigh a discovery of nature (IceCube, Higgs) above an enabling measurement invention, which is a judgement of kind on which I could be moved.
Whether the 10^-18 performance claims and the Ye credit can be confined to the lattice clock without drawing in comb, laser-stabilisation or thorium work.
statement.conflict_note: I repeat my disclosure from round 1. My profile documents a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder; Hall's 2005 recognition is adjacent to the field of B042 and Ye works in the same optical-frequency-metrology tradition, although no personal or institutional tie to Katori or Ye is documented. I do not regard this as grounds for recusal, but I leave it to the chair and committee. My ties to Lund colleagues, WACQT and Deep Light Vision bear on quantum-memory and quantum-computing candidates such as B053 and I would flag them if the discussion moved there; they do not bear on B042, B029 or B026.
